### Component
Create `apps/app/src/components/animated/animated-book/AnimatedBook.tsx`:
```tsx
'use client'

import React, { useLayoutEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import gsap from 'gsap'
import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger'
import './animated-book.css'

export type AnimatedBookProps = {
  pageCount?: number
}

export function AnimatedBook({ pageCount = 12 }: AnimatedBookProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined') return
    gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)

    const ctx = gsap.context(() => {
      const book = rootRef.current?.querySelector('.book')
      if (!book) return

      gsap.to(book, {
        scrollTrigger: {
          scrub: 1,
          start: 0,
          end: () => window.innerHeight * 0.25,
        },
        scale: 1,
      })

      const pages = Array.from(
        rootRef.current!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.book__page')
      )

      pages.forEach((page, index) => {
        gsap.set(page, { z: index === 0 ? 13 : -index })

        if (index === pageCount - 1) return

        gsap.to(page, {
          rotateY: `-=${180 - index / 2}`,
          scrollTrigger: {
            scrub: 1,
            start: () => (index + 1) * (window.innerHeight * 0.25),
            end: () => (index + 2) * (window.innerHeight * 0.25),
          },
        })

        gsap.to(page, {
          z: index === 0 ? -13 : index,
          scrollTrigger: {
            scrub: 1,
            start: () => (index + 1) * (window.innerHeight * 0.25),
            end: () => (index + 1.5) * (window.innerHeight * 0.25),
          },
        })
      })
    }, rootRef)

    return () => ctx.revert()
  }, [pageCount])

  const pages = Array.from({ length: pageCount }, (_, i) => i + 1)

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className="animated-book-root">
      <div className="book">
        <div className="book__spine" />
        {pages.map((n) => {
          const isFrontCover = n === 1
          const isBackCover = n === pageCount
          const classes = [
            'page',
            'book__page',
            isFrontCover ? 'book__cover book__cover--front' : '',
            isBackCover ? 'book__cover book__cover--back' : '',
          ]
            .filter(Boolean)
            .join(' ')

          return (
            <div
              key={n}
              className={classes}
              style={{ ['--page-index' as any]: n }}
            >
              <div className="page__half page__half--front">
                <div className="page__number">{n * 2 - 1}</div>
              </div>
              <div className="page__half page__half--back">
                <div className="page__number">{n * 2}</div>
              </div>
            </div>
          )
        })}
      </div>

      <div className="scroll-spacer" aria-hidden />
    </div>
  )
}
```

Create `apps/app/src/components/animated/animated-book/animated-book.css`:
```css
.animated-book-root {
  --page-count: 12;
  --page-scroll: 25; /* vh per segment */
  --underline: rgba(64,64,64,0.4);
  --spine: #000;
  --cover: #1a1a1a;
  --bg: #4d4d4d;
  --insert: #d9d9d9;
  --page: #e6e6e6;
  position: relative;
}

.animated-book-root .scroll-spacer {
  width: 100%;
  height: calc(((var(--page-count) + 2) * var(--page-scroll)) * 1vh);
}

.book {
  height: 40vmin;
  width: 30vmin;
  min-width: 150px;
  min-height: 200px;
  position: fixed;
  top: 50%;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(0.5);
  transform-style: preserve-3d;
  perspective: 1200px;
}

.book__spine {
  height: 100%;
  left: 0;
  top: 0;
  position: absolute;
  background: var(--spine);
  transform-origin: 0 50%;
  width: 12px;
  transform: translate3d(0, 0, -13px) scaleX(1) rotateY(0deg);
}

.book__page {
  position: absolute;
  left: 2%;
  top: 50%;
  border-radius: 0 5% 5% 0;
  transform: translate(0, -50%);
  height: 94%;
  width: 94%;
  z-index: calc(((var(--page-count) + 2) - var(--page-index)) * 2);
  transform-origin: 0% 50%;
}

.book__cover {
  border-radius: 0 5% 5% 0;
  height: 100%;
  width: 100%;
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 0;
  background: var(--cover);
}

.book__cover--front .page__half--back {
  border-right: 1rem solid var(--spine);
}

.book__cover--back .page__half--front {
  border-left: 1rem solid var(--spine);
}

.page {
  height: 100%;
  width: 100%;
  position: relative;
  transform-style: preserve-3d;
}

.page__half {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  height: 100%;
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 100%;
  transform: rotateY(calc(var(--rotation, 0) * 1deg)) translate3d(0, 0, calc((0.5 * var(--coefficient, 0)) * 1px));
  -webkit-clip-path: inset(0 0.5% 0 0.5%);
  clip-path: inset(0 0.5% 0 0.5%);
}

.page__half--front {
  --rotation: 0;
  --coefficient: 0;
  backface-visibility: hidden;
  border-radius: 0 5% 5% 0;
}

.page__half--back {
  --rotation: 180;
  --coefficient: 2;
  border-radius: 5% 0 0 5%;
}

.book__page:not(.book__cover) .page__half {
  background:
    repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 1rem, var(--underline) 1rem calc(1rem + 1px), transparent calc(1rem + 1px)) 0 1rem/100% 100% no-repeat,
    var(--page);
}

.page .page__number {
  position: absolute;
  color: #808080;
  bottom: 1rem;
  font-size: 1vmin;
}
.page__half--front .page__number { right: 1rem; }
.page__half--back .page__number { left: 1rem; }
```

# Firestarter

Firestarter instantly creates AI chatbots for any website using a modern RAG stack with streaming responses and an OpenAI‑compatible API.

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/firestarter
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firestarter-rag-chatbot-generator

## 1) Overview

- **Goal**: Enter a URL → crawl → index → chat over site content.
- **Core stack**: Next.js 15 (App Router), Vercel AI SDK (streaming), Firecrawl (crawl/clean Markdown), Upstash Search (vectors), multi‑provider LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq).
- **Outputs**:
  - Web UI for chatbot creation and querying
  - Per‑namespace RAG index
  - OpenAI‑compatible `/api/v1/chat/completions` endpoint for each chatbot

## 2) Architecture

- Crawl: Firecrawl API fetches pages → normalized Markdown
- Index: Upstash Search chunks + embeds to vectors (by namespace)
- Query: Retrieve top K chunks → system prompt → LLM → stream to UI
- Namespacing: Per chatbot isolation for documents/embeddings
- API: OpenAI‑compatible chat endpoint per namespace (model aliasing)

Sequence:
1. Submit URL → server creates namespace
2. Firecrawl crawl job → Markdown pages
3. Index to Upstash Search (chunk+embed)
4. UI/SDK queries → retrieve → LLM → stream

## 3) Prerequisites

- Node 18+ / Bun ok if repo supports
- Accounts/keys:
  - Firecrawl API
  - Upstash Search (REST URL/token)
  - At least one LLM provider key (OpenAI or Anthropic or Groq)
- Vercel optional (recommended)

## 4) Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mendableai/firestarter
cd firestarter
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
# Fill keys
npm run dev
```

### 4.1 Environment

```
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=...
UPSTASH_SEARCH_REST_URL=...
UPSTASH_SEARCH_REST_TOKEN=...
# Pick at least one:
OPENAI_API_KEY=...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
GROQ_API_KEY=...
```

### 4.2 Configuration

`firestarter.config.ts` controls crawl limits, provider priority, and feature flags (e.g., enableCreation). Adjust namespace policies and retrieval params (topK, similarity threshold) as needed.

## 5) Usage

- Visit `http://localhost:3000`
- Create chatbot: enter URL → start → wait for crawl/index
- Query: ask questions in UI; responses stream
- Programmatic: use OpenAI SDK with baseURL to Firestarter’s `/api/v1/chat/completions`, model name = generated namespace alias.

Example (JS):
```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'any', // Firestarter handles auth server-side
  baseURL: 'https://your-firestarter.vercel.app/api/v1/chat/completions'
})

const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'firecrawl-example-com-12345',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'What is Firecrawl?' }],
})
console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content)
```

## 6) RAG Configuration

- Chunk size/overlap: tune per content type (docs vs blogs)
- Embeddings model: pick provider that matches Upstash Search defaults
- Retrieval: topK 4–12 typical; raise for longer answers
- Prompting: keep system prompt “grounded; cite sources; no hallucinations”
- Namespace TTL: optional cleanup policy for ephemeral bots

## 7) MCP and Context7 Integration

- Firecrawl MCP:
  - Use MCP tool for URL ingestion and crawl status retrieval.
  - Recommended workflow: enqueue crawl → poll status → write normalized Markdown into Firestarter ingestion pipeline (or directly to Upstash Search; ensure namespace consistency).
- Context7:
  - Use as external knowledge context provider; forward retrieved chunks from Context7 to Firestarter’s LLM layer (bypassing internal retrieval) by plugging into the “retrieval override” hook.
- Suggested server action:
  - Implement a Server Action `ingestExternalDocs({ namespace, docs[] })` to accept pre‑scraped items from MCP/Context7 jobs.

## 8) Deployment

- Vercel: zero‑config Next.js + serverless functions
- Set env vars in Vercel dashboard
- Increase crawl limits for self‑hosted (see `firestarter.config.ts`)
- CDN/Edge cache UI, keep API dynamic
- Scale: Upstash Search is serverless; Firecrawl is external SaaS

## 9) Observability

- Log: request ids, namespace, provider, tokens used
- Metrics: crawl durations, indexing throughput, search latency, tokens per answer
- Traces: enable Vercel AI SDK events, LLM streaming markers

## 10) Security & Compliance

- Verify domain ownership for public deployments to prevent abuse
- Rate‑limit chatbot creation and query endpoints
- Respect robots.txt and site TOS in crawling
- PII: avoid persisting chats by default; redact logs

## 11) Troubleshooting

- Crawl returns empty: verify Firecrawl key and robots.txt
- No results: confirm namespace and that indexing completed
- 401 on API: baseURL correct, deployment URL matches
- Slow answers: reduce topK or chunk size; check provider latency
- Hallucinations: tighten prompt; lower temperature; increase grounding

## 12) Roadmap (suggested)

- Multi‑tenancy auth + quotas
- Per‑namespace prompt/versioning
- Source highlighting inline
- Feedback loop (helpfulness, citations valid)

## 13) References

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/firestarter
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firestarter-rag-chatbot-generator
```

# Firecrawl Observer

Monitor any web page for content changes with visual diffs and intelligent alerts.

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/firecrawl-observer
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-firecrawl-observer

## 1) Overview

- **Goal**: Track changes on target URLs; be notified when meaningful updates occur.
- **Core stack**: Next.js + Convex (as referenced), Firecrawl for fetch/normalize, AI significance scoring, visual diff viewer.
- **Use cases**: Docs updates, pricing pages, product changes, government releases.

## 2) Architecture

- Scheduler triggers fetch via Firecrawl
- Normalize content → markdown/blocks
- Diff engine produces semantic/visual diff
- AI significance filter classifies “trivial” vs “meaningful”
- Notification channels: email/webhook; UI dashboard

## 3) Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mendableai/firecrawl-observer
cd firecrawl-observer
npm install
cp .env.local.example .env.local
# Fill keys (Firecrawl, email/webhook providers, Convex if used)
npm run dev
```

### 3.1 Environment

Common variables:
```
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=...
NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL=...
EMAIL_PROVIDER_KEY=...
CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT=... # if applicable
```

## 4) Usage

- Add URL monitor with schedule (seconds → weeks)
- Choose change scope (full page vs selector subset)
- Configure notifications (webhook/email)
- Review diff: side‑by‑side HTML/Markdown; view AI summary

## 5) Diffing & Significance

- Heuristics: ignore timestamps, counters, A/B fragments
- AI layer: model classifies change significance and tags summary
- Thresholds: adjustable for sensitivity (e.g., ignore < N characters)

## 6) MCP and Context7 Integration

- Firecrawl MCP:
  - Use MCP to batch‑register monitors; store job ids; standardized crawl payloads for reproducibility.
- Context7:
  - Push diffs to Context7 as “events” for downstream research; embed event payload (old/new snippets, URL, time).
- Suggested webhooks:
  - `POST /api/observer/webhook` receives change events with `{ url, detectedAt, significance, summary, diffUrl }`.

## 7) Deployment

- Self‑host (Vercel/Node runtime). Ensure scheduler/cron is configured.
- Persist history (Convex/DB): store snapshots, diffs, labels.
- Secrets via env; rotate keys.

## 8) Observability

- Metrics: checks per hour, success rate, average fetch time
- Alerts: repeated failures per URL
- Audit: change history export (CSV/JSON)

## 9) Security

- Rate limits per origin
- Respect robots.txt and cache headers
- Allowlist for internal deployments

## 10) Troubleshooting

- Frequent false positives: expand ignore selectors; raise thresholds
- Missing changes: lower thresholds; ensure route not client‑rendered only
- 4xx/5xx: check target site anti‑bot rules; apply polite headers/backoff
- Email not delivered: verify provider and domain settings

## 11) Roadmap (suggested)

- Per‑selector diff granularity
- Screenshot diff layer
- Multi‑tenant/projects
- SLA alerts (critical pages)

## 12) References

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/firecrawl-observer
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-firecrawl-observer
```

# Open Researcher

Real‑time thinking, split‑view analysis, and automatic citations for deep web research.

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/open-researcher
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/open-researcher-interleaved-thinking

## 1) Overview

- **Goal**: Provide transparent, sourced research with live reasoning and side‑by‑side evidence.
- **Core stack**: Next.js UI + Firecrawl (fetch), Claude/OpenAI/Groq (LLMs), Vercel AI SDK (stream), citation builder.
- **Unique**: Interleaved thinking (exposes planning vs synthesis), auto citations, multi‑pane reading.

## 2) Architecture

- Query planner generates sub‑tasks
- Retriever fetches web sources (via Firecrawl)
- Reader ranks snippets → context window
- LLM composes answer with citations; thoughts rendered live
- UI panes: results list, active sources, draft, final

## 3) Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mendableai/open-researcher
cd open-researcher
npm install
cp .env.local.example .env.local
# Fill LLM keys + Firecrawl
npm run dev
```

### 3.1 Environment

```
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=...
OPENAI_API_KEY=... # or
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... # or
GROQ_API_KEY=...
```

## 4) Usage

- Enter research question
- Watch planner → retrieval → drafting with live tokens
- Inspect sources; open split view to compare claims
- Export answer + citations (markdown)

## 5) Prompting & Citations

- System prompt enforces: “Use only cited sources; avoid speculation”
- Auto‑citation format: `[n] Title (domain) – URL`
- Deduplicate sources and include access timestamps
- Temperature low for factual synthesis

## 6) MCP and Context7 Integration

- Firecrawl MCP:
  - Batch ingest curated corpora (PDFs, docs sites) as pre‑indexed sources.
- Context7:
  - Use as external memory store for previous findings; seed planner with prior nodes.
- Hook:
  - `ingestExternalSources({ topicId, docs[] })` server action to register external artifacts and citations.

## 7) Deployment

- Vercel recommended; enable streaming
- Configure domain/cors for browser source previews
- Persist research sessions for auditability (optional)

## 8) Observability

- Track tokens, provider, latency
- Log citations per answer
- Error budgets for failed fetches

## 9) Security & Ethics

- Respect site terms and robots.txt
- Cite all claims; mark uncertainty
- Disallow unsafe content; filter PII

## 10) Troubleshooting

- Empty results: broaden query; verify Firecrawl
- Hallucinations: strengthen instruction; increase retrieved K; lower temp
- Broken citations: validate URLs; re‑rank snippets

## 11) Roadmap (suggested)

- Multi‑agent debate
- Judgment with toolformer feedback
- Workspace memory graph
- Rich PDF ingestion pipeline

## 12) References

- Repo: https://github.com/mendableai/open-researcher
- Blog: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/open-researcher-interleaved-thinking
```

### Exa Search API quick integration

- **Docs link**: [Exa Search API reference](https://docs.exa.ai/reference/search?auth_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJuYW1lIjoiTGlhbSBFbGxpcyIsImVtYWlsIjoibGlhbUBsaWFtZWxsaXMuZGV2IiwiYXBpS2V5IjoiY2Q0MDNhNGUtYWYyMy00ZjI3LWIxMDctZWI3M2JkODE1YThjIiwidmVyc2lvbiI6MSwiaWF0IjoxNzU0ODQyMjIwfQ.jnCUxE7io1kn5x7GfoGhS8KkrU4L79sqavoxnGGOwHM)

- **Endpoint**: `POST https://api.exa.ai/search`
- **Auth**: header `x-api-key: YOUR-EXA-API-KEY`
- **Common payload**:
  - `query: string`
  - `text: true` to include extracted page text
- **Response**: `results[]` with `title`, `url`, `publishedDate`, `text` (if requested), `highlights`, `summary`, `subpages`, etc.

Code samples

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://api.exa.ai/search' \
  -H 'x-api-key: $EXA_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Latest research in LLMs","text":true}'
```

```ts
// TypeScript (Next.js/Node)
const EXA_API = 'https://api.exa.ai/search'

type ExaSearchResult = {
  title: string
  url: string
  publishedDate?: string
  text?: string
  highlights?: string[]
  summary?: string
  subpages?: Array<{ url: string; title?: string; text?: string }>
}

export async function exaSearch(query: string, withText = true) {
  const res = await fetch(EXA_API, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'x-api-key': process.env.EXA_API_KEY!,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, text: withText }),
  })
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Exa search failed: ${res.status}`)
  const data = await res.json()
  return (data.results || []) as ExaSearchResult[]
}
```

Integration tips

- **Open Researcher**: use `text` and `summary` fields as retrieval snippets; map to citations `{title, url, publishedDate}` and render highlights in split view. Lower temperature; enforce “answers must cite.”
- **Firestarter**: use Exa to discover relevant URLs, then hand URLs to your crawler/indexer (Firecrawl) by namespace before chatbot creation, or ingest Exa `text` directly if you trust extraction.
- **Observer**: seed monitored URL sets from Exa queries; store `url` + `publishedDate` to prioritize fresh sources.

Notes

- Keep `EXA_API_KEY` in env; never commit tokens.
- For larger excerpts, prefer setting `text: true` on search results to avoid separate fetches.
- Review Exa pricing fields in the response (`costDollars`) to budget calls.

Reference

- Exa Search API: [docs.exa.ai/reference/search](https://docs.exa.ai/reference/search?auth_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJuYW1lIjoiTGlhbSBFbGxpcyIsImVtYWlsIjoibGlhbUBsaWFtZWxsaXMuZGV2IiwiYXBpS2V5IjoiY2Q0MDNhNGUtYWYyMy00ZjI3LWIxMDctZWI3M2JkODE1YThjIiwidmVyc2lvbiI6MSwiaWF0IjoxNzU0ODQyMjIwfQ.jnCUxE7io1kn5x7GfoGhS8KkrU4L79sqavoxnGGOwHM)

- Changes
